messages.subject: Overlapping Boxplot and Line + extras
parts:
Dear All,
I am trying to combine different geometries but I am experiencing some
difficulties (probably I have not yet properly understood the layer
mechanism).
Consider the following code snippet at the end of this email.
I am trying simply to combine a boxplot and a line or a line and some
points together, but the 'combined' plots always fail for a reason or
another...
(1) Can anyone help me out with them? I am puzzled because I (think that
I) am following
suggestion 2 in http://tinyurl.com/y8v2aoq , but without the same
success obviously.
(2) Can anyone add a legend to the plots combining two geometries with
any two names for the two quantities of interest? Then I will try to do
my best to modify the legend according to my needs.
(3) I am trying to use ggplot2 to generate some figure which should end
up in a presentation with a black background (using latex and beamer).
If the figures are "transparent", then they will be invisible or
partially covered by the black background.
With base graphics I used to supply the parameter bg='white' within
'plot' when generating the figures to fix this, but I am not sure about
how to proceed here.
Can anyone point me to the right direction?
Many thanks

Lorenzo

set.seed(1234)

n_tot <- rep(seq(100,300,by=50),100)
n_inf <- 200+abs(rnorm(length(n_tot),0,20))

n_inf[which(n_inf<100)] <- 100
n_inf[which(n_inf>300)] <- 300


my_dframe <- data.frame(cbind(n_tot,n_inf))
names(my_dframe) <- c("n_tot","n_inf")
my_dframe$n_tot <- factor(my_dframe$n_tot)

data_max <- data.frame(cbind(unique(n_tot),unique(n_tot)))

names(data_max) <- c("n_tot_x","n_tot_y")

gpl <- ggplot(my_dframe,aes(x=n_tot,y=n_inf ))+
geom_boxplot()+

## scale_x_log10() +
## scale_y_log10()+
## scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,.3))+
## scale_y_continuous(trans = "log10")+

xlab(expression(paste("Number of visitors")))+
ylab(expression(paste("Distribution Infected Visitors")))+
opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 20))+
opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 20, angle=90))+
opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size=15, colour="gray",vjust=1))+
opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size=15, colour="gray", hjust=1))

fn <- paste("box_plot_ggplot2.pdf")

pdf(fn)
print(gpl)
dev.off()


gpl_line <- ggplot(data_max,aes(x=n_tot_x,y=n_tot_y ))+geom_line()


fn <- paste("ggplot2_line.pdf")

pdf(fn)
print(gpl_line)
dev.off()

#Now I try some combined plots


new_overlay <- ggplot() +
geom_boxplot(data=my_dframe, aes(x=n_tot,y=n_inf )) +
geom_line(data=data_max,aes(x=n_tot_x,y=n_tot_y ), colour="red" )

fn <- paste("box_plot_line_overlay_ggplot2.pdf")

pdf(fn)
print(new_overlay)
dev.off()


new_overlay <- ggplot() +
geom_point(data_max,aes(x=n_tot_x,y=n_tot_y)) +
geom_line(data=data_max,aes(x=n_tot_x,y=n_tot_y ), colour="red" )


fn <- paste("point_line_overlay_ggplot2.pdf")

pdf(fn)
print(new_overlay)
dev.off()

Dear All,
I am trying to combine different geometries but I am experiencing some difficulties (probably I have not yet properly understood the layer mechanism).
Consider the following code snippet at the end of this email.
I am trying simply to combine a boxplot and a line or a line and some points together, but the 'combined' plots always fail for a reason or another...
(1) Can anyone help me out with them? I am puzzled because I (think that I) am following
suggestion 2 in http://tinyurl.com/y8v2aoq , but without the same success obviously.
(2) Can anyone add a legend to the plots combining two geometries with any two names for the two quantities of interest? Then I will try to do my best to modify the legend according to my needs.
(3) I am trying to use ggplot2 to generate some figure which should end up in a presentation with a black background (using latex and beamer).
If the figures are "transparent", then they will be invisible or partially covered by the black background.
With base graphics I used to supply the parameter bg='white' within 'plot' when generating the figures to fix this, but I am not sure about how to proceed here.
Can anyone point me to the right direction?
Many thanks

Lorenzo

set.seed(1234)

n_tot <- rep(seq(100,300,by=50),100)
n_inf <- 200+abs(rnorm(length(n_tot),0,20))

n_inf[which(n_inf<100)] <- 100
n_inf[which(n_inf>300)] <- 300


my_dframe <- data.frame(cbind(n_tot,n_inf))
names(my_dframe) <- c("n_tot","n_inf")
my_dframe$n_tot <- factor(my_dframe$n_tot)

data_max <- data.frame(cbind(unique(n_tot),unique(n_tot)))

names(data_max) <- c("n_tot_x","n_tot_y")

gpl <- ggplot(my_dframe,aes(x=n_tot,y=n_inf ))+
 geom_boxplot()+

 ## scale_x_log10() +
 ## scale_y_log10()+
 ## scale_y_continuous(limits=c(0,.3))+
 ## scale_y_continuous(trans = "log10")+

In your xlab and ylab statements, you have no expression, only text, so
xlab("Number of visitors") + ylab("Distribution infected visitors")
is sufficient.

xlab(expression(paste("Number of visitors")))+
 ylab(expression(paste("Distribution Infected Visitors")))+
 opts(axis.title.x = theme_text(size = 20))+
 opts(axis.title.y = theme_text(size = 20, angle=90))+
 opts(axis.text.x = theme_text(size=15, colour="gray",vjust=1))+
 opts(axis.text.y = theme_text(size=15, colour="gray", hjust=1))
So far, so good; I got the boxplots using my modified xlab and ylab.

fn <- paste("box_plot_ggplot2.pdf")

pdf(fn)
print(gpl)
dev.off()


gpl_line <- ggplot(data_max,aes(x=n_tot_x,y=n_tot_y ))+geom_line()


fn <- paste("ggplot2_line.pdf")

pdf(fn)
print(gpl_line)
dev.off()

#Now I try some combined plots


new_overlay <- ggplot() +
geom_boxplot(data=my_dframe, aes(x=n_tot,y=n_inf )) +
geom_line(data=data_max,aes(x=n_tot_x,y=n_tot_y ), colour="red" )

Some definite problems here. Your call generates
> new_overlay <- ggplot() +

> new_overlay
Error: Non-continuous variable supplied to scale_x_continuous.

There are two problems that I can see:

(1) In my_dframe, n_tot is a factor, but in data_max, n_tot is numeric.
     Same variable, different classes -> clash, which is possibly what
     generated the error message.

(2) In the boxplots, the vertical scale of n_inf ranges from 200 to 268,
     but in the line plot, the vertical scale ranges from 100 to 300.

fn <- paste("box_plot_line_overlay_ggplot2.pdf")

pdf(fn)
print(new_overlay)
dev.off()


new_overlay <- ggplot() +
geom_point(data_max,aes(x=n_tot_x,y=n_tot_y)) +
 geom_line(data=data_max,aes(x=n_tot_x,y=n_tot_y ), colour="red" )

Running this code generates the following error:
> new_overlay <- ggplot() +
+ geom_point(data_max,aes(x=n_tot_x,y=n_tot_y)) +

Error: ggplot2 doesn't know how to deal with data of class uneval

...but this works...
 ggplot(data_max,aes(x=n_tot_x,y=n_tot_y)) + geom_line() + geom_point()


My attempt to put the two together started by changing n_tot in my_dframe
from factor to numeric:

my_dframe$n_tot <- as.numeric(as.character(my_dframe$n_tot))

This got me the boxplots:
ggplot(my_dframe, aes(x = n_tot, y = n_inf, group = n_tot)) + geom_boxplot()

I then tried to superimpose the line; I got the vertical scales to expand, and
the boxplots look OK, but the line wasn't drawn. This is what I tried:

p + geom_line(data = data_max, aes(x = n_tot_x, y = n_tot_y, colour = 'red'))

The boxplots and a legend item for 'red' showed up, but that was it.

Hopefully someone else can complete this; I am not yet that conversant in ggplot2
to figure out the remaining steps.

Hope this helps,
Dennis
